title: Lesson 84 - I'm Following Up in Writing

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: I’m calling before I close CVR-2086. The replacement was returned Thursday at 4:40, the proposed hold was removed Wednesday at 8:55 and no damage fee will be charged.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Thank you. I also completed the client review on Wednesday. I’m following up in writing because the automated email describes the replacement as “accepted in settlement of the damage charge.”

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: That is not an accurate description. There was no damage charge to settle, and you accepted the replacement as an operational remedy while the cause review continued.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: That’s not how the phone agreement was explained to me either. Can we compare the automated sentence with the conditional agreement and final claims note?

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: Yes. The conditional agreement says the replacement did not determine responsibility. The final note says the physical evidence was insufficient to classify the damage as customer-caused.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Does the final note say the courier caused it?

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: No. It says the damage pattern is consistent with compression through the lower-right corner, but the records do not establish the exact stage or responsible party.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Then the written correction should include both limits: no customer damage charge and no finding against a specific courier or warehouse employee.

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: Agreed. Let me summarize where we are: service access was restored, both units were returned, the account was corrected and the cause remains unassigned.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Before we move on, please add that the Wednesday–Thursday rental window and all transport were provided without an extra charge.

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: I’ll replace the automated phrase with: “A same-model replacement was provided as an interim service remedy. No customer damage charge was applied.”

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: My understanding is that the case can now close even though the company did not identify the exact damage stage. Is that correct?

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: Correct. Closing the service case records the account decision and completed remedy; it does not create a technical finding the evidence cannot support.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: The following points should be marked closed: replacement delivery, damaged-unit collection, rental-window reset, replacement return and removal of the proposed hold.

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: The only non-finding is responsibility for the original damage. There are no remaining customer actions or amounts due under this order.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Could we bring this back to the main point of the final email? A reader should know what happened, what was decided and what was not decided without reopening every phone call.

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: Then the email will contain a six-line timeline, the evidence conclusion, the account decision, the non-finding and a request for correction within two business days.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Please correct anything I have misunderstood: the technical report narrowed the mechanism, Claims found insufficient evidence for customer-caused damage and ClearView chose not to charge me.

lines.speaker: Daria
lines.text: That is accurate. I’ll send the final case record today and keep the correction channel open for two business days before the file becomes read-only.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Is that an accurate record of the decision? The service dispute is closed, no money or action remains due from me and the exact damage responsibility was not determined.

transfer.title: Eli's technical assessment message
transfer.instruction: Listen twice without reading. Record the inspected parts, supported mechanism, absent customer-use signs, unresolved stage and reporting limit before giving a neutral 60-second summary.
transfer.speaker: Eli
